theater: 寧夏靈州、第五都與黃河渡口

battle.name: 靈州之戰
battle.theater: 寧夏靈州、第五都與黃河渡口
battle.brief: 元豐四年，宋神宗以五路大軍伐西夏，環慶、涇原兩路合攻黃河東岸的靈州，四月至五月間城破；宋軍進抵黃河對岸，兵鋒已及興慶府門外，卻因糧道被騎兵切斷、河東路全軍覆於第五都而被迫撤退，靈州仍歸西夏。卡面的希臘火不在這個內陸戰場上，同期可與之對照的，是東方火矢與猛火油柜的普及。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 一〇八一年的靈州之戰，是北宋與西夏之間宋夏戰爭的最高潮，也是宋神宗元豐年間五路伐夏中最關鍵的一場。交戰雙方的體系差異很大。宋朝方面由皇帝趙頊直接拍板，以王韶為五路大軍總統，坐鎮京師遙制，前線分熙河、鄜延、河東、環慶、涇原五路推進，各路經略使就地指揮；兵員以募兵為主，禁軍精銳與西北邊軍為骨幹，步軍結陣，騎兵擔任機動，另有招撫吐蕃部落編成蕃兵與熟戶充當嚮導。糧秣自京師輾轉運至涇原、環慶的倉場，再以車隊北運。西夏方面正處在諒祚與其母沒臧氏爭權之後的動盪期，樞密院掌握兵權，境內以御營與宿衛的精騎為核心，防線上則是漢兵與橫山羌兵分編的邊軍，槍手、駙手、弓箭手各部自成建制，另有具甲衝鋒用的鐵鷂子。靈州一線是西夏的農業區與門戶，控扼黃河東岸的渡口，漢人與羌人雜居，城中既屯糧又屯兵。西夏的戰略是集中精兵於靈州周邊，以騎兵速度對付分散五路的宋軍，同時派遊騎切斷宋軍糧道。外部環境上，遼國在燕雲一線保持壓迫而未大舉出兵，吐蕃木征部落在熙河方向牽制宋軍，雙方才能把主力壓到西北一線，這場戰爭才打得成雙方傾盡所力的樣子。
countriesEn: The Battle of Lingzhou in 1081 was the climax of the Song–Western Xia war and the decisive engagement of the five-pronged offensive launched by Emperor Shenzong in the Yuanfeng era. The two sides were organised in very different ways. On the Song side the decision was taken by the emperor himself, Zhao Xu, who appointed Wang Shao as president of the five armies and sat in the capital directing them by written order, while five routes — Xihé, Fuyan, Hedong, Huanqing and Jingyuan — advanced under their own regional commanders. Troops were raised by recruitment: the imperial guards and the frontier armies of the northwest formed the core, infantry fought in line, cavalry provided the mobility, and there were also native recruits and settled households drawn from Tibetan tribes who served as guides. Grain and provisions were shifted from the capital in long convoys to the depots of Jingyuan and Huanqing and then carted north. On the Western Xia side the year belonged to the turbulent period after the struggle between Liangzuo and his mother, the Empress Dowager Maozang: the Privy Council held the military power, the imperial camp and the guard formed the elite core, and the frontier was manned by Han troops and Hengshan Qiang troops organised separately, with spearmen, lancers and archers each forming their own units, while armoured lancers such as the Tiejiaozi served as shock troops. Lingzhou was Western Xia's farming district and its gateway, commanding the fords of the eastern bank of the Yellow River, with Han and Qiang populations mixed in the city, which stored grain and quartered troops. Western Xia's plan was to concentrate the best cavalry around Lingzhou, to use their speed against the Song's dispersed five routes, and to send out mobile raiding parties to cut the Song supply lines. In the wider setting, the Liao dynasty exerted pressure along the Yanyun frontier without committing large forces, and the Tibetan leader Muzheng held the Song in check in the Xihé direction, so that each side could concentrate its main body in the northwest; that is what allowed the war to be fought with everything each side could muster.
people: 宋方最關鍵的決策者是神宗趙頊。元豐四年他把西北用兵提升到國家最高的戰略層次，批准王韶的方略，以五路大軍直取西夏的核心，而不是像先前那樣只在邊境做堡寨羈縻之爭；詔令下達、五路出師、糧運分派、撤軍時機，全由他在汴京控制。統帥王韶是熙河開闢的主將，熟悉西北地形與部族，他主張先取河湟、斷西夏與吐蕃的聯絡，再圖靈州，位置因此偏在後方居中調度。前線出力的人各有分工：熙河一路由種詡領兵，向河湟與洮峽的吐蕃聚落推進，逼迫木征部退入山地；涇原一路以劉昌祚為主將，負責正面進逼靈州；河東一路的徐禧率軍出河套追擊，攻下靈州之後把兵鋒推向無定河上游的第五都，同年秋全軍覆沒，徐禧與隨騎數十人戰死；此外還有環慶、鄜延兩路的指揮官，環慶一路是靈州攻城的另一支主力，鄜延一路向米脂、綏德一線施壓，企圖切斷西夏與契丹邊界的往來。西夏方面的關鍵人物是諒祚，他在幽禁母后沒臧氏、清除一批反對的臣將之後才真正掌握軍權，靈州與河套的防務由樞密院直接調度；具體統兵者多見於漢將與羌首，橫山一帶的羌首在守城與反擊中扮演了不亞於漢兵的角色，因為他們熟悉黃河灘地與套內道路。
peopleEn: On the Song side the decisive figure was the emperor, Shenzong, Zhao Xu. In the Yuanfeng era he raised operations in the northwest to the level of national strategy, approved Wang Shao's plan, and put five armies into the field against the heart of Western Xia instead of merely building forts and holding nominal control along the frontier. The edicts, the deployment of the five routes, the allocation of transport and the timing of the withdrawal were all in his hands at Bianjing. The overall commander, Wang Shao, was the man who had opened up Xihé, and he knew the northwestern terrain and the tribal politics intimately; he argued for taking Hedong and cutting Western Xia off from the Tibetans before moving on Lingzhou, which placed him behind the lines in a coordinating role. Among those who did the fighting in front, the division of labour was clear. Zhong Xu led the Xihé route, driving the Tibetan strongholds of Hedong and the Tao gorges and pressing Muzheng's people back into the mountains. Liu Changzuo commanded the Jingyuan route, responsible for the direct pressure on Lingzhou. Xu Xi led the Hedong route out of the Hetao, followed up after Lingzhou fell and pushed his head towards Fifth Prefecture on the upper reaches of the Wuding, where in the autumn of 1081 the whole force was destroyed and Xu Xi was killed with a few dozen riders. The commanders of the Huanqing and Fuyan routes formed the rest of the command: Huanqing was the other main arm of the assault on Lingzhou, while Fuyan pressed on the Mizhi–Suide line in an attempt to sever Western Xia's links with the Khitan border. On the Western Xia side the key figure was Liangzuo, who only gained real control of the army after shutting away his mother, the Empress Dowager Maozang, and purging the courtiers who opposed him; the defence of Lingzhou and the Hetao was directed by the Privy Council. The commanders in the field were largely Han generals and Qiang chieftains, and the chieftains of the Hengshan area played a role no smaller than the Han troops in holding the city and counterattacking, because they knew the Yellow River flats and the tracks inside the loop of the river better than anyone.
kits: 這張卡面上的希臘火在靈州戰場上並不存在，這一點必須先說清楚：它是七世紀拜占庭帝國的秘密武器，裝在銅管裡，由船上的操作手以人力泵推送，在水面或牆根噴出難以熄滅的燃燒劑，配方與器具都由帝國中樞壟斷而不外傳；紀錄始於七世紀末對阿拉伯海軍的攻擊，此後在拜占庭與阿拉伯的戰爭中反覆出現，到十二世紀初已近乎絕跡，連十字軍東征時代常被影射為它大顯神威的說法，多數研究也認為出自傳聞。一〇八一年的靈州是內陸的黃河東岸，沒有拜占庭式的艦隊，也不存在國家壟斷的燃燒兵種，東西兩相隔四千餘里。真正可以對照的，是同期東方兵器圖籍中記載的猛火油柜一類噴射器械：用管盛放油膏，能把燃燒的液體射向城樓、船只或人群，原理與希臘火同屬把燃燒劑儲存在管中再壓出，但用途限於攻守器械，並無專門的操作兵種，也沒有帝國級別的保密。戰場上真正起作用的是火藥與火箭：火矢用來燒敵陣、燒草車、擾亂攻城隊形，煙火一類的砲用於遮蔽和驅散密集隊形，此外還有神臂弓這類強弩，是宋軍攻城與野戰中最被倚重的遠程火力。西夏一方則有具甲的鐵鷂子精騎，以及弓弩與長刀，攻守都倚重騎兵的速度與機動。攻城器械方面，宋軍備有撞車、雲梯、對樓、望車與飛石，渡黃河靠浮橋與舟筏，糧秣運轉以車隊為主，近線的補給交給步夫。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card was not present on the field of Lingzhou, and that has to be said first. Greek fire was the secret weapon of the seventh-century Byzantine Empire, carried in bronze tubes, driven by an operator on the ship with a hand pump, and projecting a burning charge that was hard to extinguish; the formula and the apparatus were held by the imperial centre and never given out. The earliest records date to the attacks on the Arab fleets at the end of the seventh century, it reappeared repeatedly in Byzantine wars against the Arabs, and by the early twelfth century it had very nearly vanished; even the popular picture of it doing great deeds at the time of the Crusades is, in the judgement of most scholars, largely hearsay. Lingzhou in 1081 stood on the eastern bank of the Yellow River far inland; there was no Byzantine fleet there and no state-monopoly corps of flame, and the two were more than four thousand kilometres apart. What can honestly be set against it is the class of projection devices recorded in the Chinese weapons manuals of the same century: the menghuoyougui, a container of oil or grease with a tube that could spray burning liquid at a tower, a boat or a mass of men. The principle is the same as Greek fire — storing a burning charge in a tube and forcing it out — but its use was confined to siege and boarding equipment, there was no dedicated crew for it, and it was never guarded as an imperial secret. What actually mattered on the battlefield was gunpowder and fire arrows: fire arrows burned up enemy formations, grass carts and the approach of the assaulting columns, while smoke bombs of the thunder-crack type were used to screen movement and break up massed formations; alongside these stood the Shenbi crossbow, a powerful drawn bow that gave the Song army its most trusted long-range fire both in the field and before the walls. Western Xia on the other side had armoured cavalry in the Tiejiaozi, and bows, crossbows and long sabres, and built its offence and defence on the speed and mobility of horsemen. For siege work the Song brought battering rams, ladders, siege towers, observation cars and stone-throwers; to cross the Yellow River they used pontoon bridges and rafts; and the moving of grain and provisions was done above all by cart, with footmen carrying what the carts could not reach.
tactics: 宋軍的戰術是一場典型的分進合擊：五路之中，環慶與涇原兩路夾擊靈州，鄜延一路壓向米脂、綏德，切斷西夏與契丹邊界的聯繫，熙河一路在河湟驅逐吐蕃木征部，河東一路則準備渡過黃河掃蕩套內的殘餘據點；靈州是五路會合的樞紐，也是西夏在河套的門戶。攻城方式是宋軍的老辦法：先屯營紮營，築壕溝、立木柵與拒馬，把城外地盤一點點吃乾淨，同時用遠程弓弩與砲火壓制城頭，限制守軍出城反擊，再填壕架雲梯、推撞車攻門。西夏的反擊重點不在守城而在反攻：精騎集中於靈州城內與城郊，一旦宋軍的攻城部隊離開營盤、糧隊落在後方，便以騎兵疾馳插入其側背，切斷糧道；河東路宋軍攻下靈州後追擊過頭，全軍在第五都遭騎兵包圍而覆沒，正是這一套打法最有效的一擊。宋軍在靈州周邊也曾以火矢與油膏噴射器械攻擊城樓與拒馬，用焚燒配合強攻，但這類手段規模有限，更像攻城器械的補充而非獨立的破城手段。撤退同樣是戰術的一部分：詔令撤兵時，諸路焚燬攻城器械與屯積糧草，只留少數駐軍據點，分道退回環慶、鄜延一線，避免在西夏騎兵隨時能咬住的黃河灘頭上被追上。
tacticsEn: The Song plan was a classic convergent attack. Of the five routes, Huanqing and Jingyuan struck at Lingzhou together, Fuyan pressed towards Mizhi and Suide to cut Western Xia off from the Khitan border, Xihé drove the Tibetans of Muzheng back through Hedong, and Hedong was to cross the Yellow River and clear the remaining strongholds inside the loop of the river; Lingzhou was the hinge where the five routes were to join, and the gateway of Western Xia to the Hetao. The method of taking the city was the standard Song method. The troops first made camp and dug in, filling in a trench and planting wooden fences and caltrops to take the ground outside the walls piece by piece, while long-range bows, crossbows and artillery fire kept the parapets pinned down and discouraged the garrison from sallying out; then the trench was filled, ladders were raised against the walls and rams were driven against the gates. Western Xia's reply lay not in holding the city but in counterattacking. The best cavalry were concentrated in and around Lingzhou, and the moment a Song assault group left its camp or a supply column fell behind, horsemen would ride in against the flank and rear and cut the road; the annihilation of the Hedong route at Fifth Prefecture, after it had overreached in pursuit, was the single most effective application of that method. The Song also tried fire arrows and oil-spraying devices against towers and barricades at Lingzhou, using burning to assist the assault, but such measures were limited in scale and served as an adjunct to siege equipment rather than a means of taking the city on their own. Withdrawal was likewise a tactical problem: when the order to retreat came, the various routes burned their siege equipment and the grain they had piled up, left only small garrison posts, and withdrew by separate lines back towards Huanqing and Fuyan rather than risk being caught on the Yellow River flats where Western Xia horsemen could always take a bite out of them.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時間線：元豐四年二月神宗下詔，五路大軍三月出師，四月進抵靈州城下，四月至五月間靈州城被攻破，同年夏秋河東路追擊至第五都而覆沒，九月詔令各路撤退。兵力：五路出兵的總數在數十萬一級，常見說法稱四十餘萬，但各路數目互有出入，保存下來的多是各路自報的額度。糧秣：出師之前宋廷在涇原、環慶一線屯積大批軍糧，再以車隊北運，運量以數十萬石計，運距越長，前線的饑餓壓力越大。損失：史籍明確記載的最大一次打擊是第五都之敗，河東路一部全軍覆沒，徐禧與數十騎死於亂軍，隨軍官員與兵員被俘、被殺與潰散者甚眾。戰果：靈州一度為宋軍所占，兵鋒直抵黃河對岸，興慶府的城郭已近在河那一邊；但宋軍最終未能守住占領區，撤退之後靈州仍歸西夏治理。戰役整體歷時約半年，跨二月至九月。關於戰俘與攻城細節的記載多已散佚，數字不可逐條核實，因此凡涉及具體人數與物資的條目，只採可以互相印證的量級說法，不作精確斷言。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The timeline: in the second month of the Yuanfeng era the emperor issued the edict, the five routes marched in the third month, reached the walls of Lingzhou in the fourth, and the city was stormed between the fourth and fifth months; in the late summer and autumn of the same year the Hedong route was destroyed in the pursuit towards Fifth Prefecture, and in the ninth month the order to withdraw was issued. Strength: the total of the five armies was of the order of several hundred thousand; the figure usually given is over four hundred thousand, but the numbers for the individual routes differ, and what has survived is mostly each route's own estimate. Provisions: before the army set out the court piled up large stocks of grain along the Jingyuan and Huanqing lines and had them carted north, the quantities being counted in hundreds of thousands of bushels; the longer the haul, the greater the hunger at the front. Losses: the single greatest blow recorded in the histories is the defeat at Fifth Prefecture, where the whole Hedong force was destroyed, Xu Xi and a few dozen riders died in the rout, and officers and men were killed, taken prisoner or scattered in large numbers. Gains: Lingzhou was for a time held by the Song, whose advanced posts reached the far bank of the Yellow River with the walls of Xingqing close on the other side; but the Song could not hold what it had taken, and after the withdrawal Lingzhou returned to Western Xia administration. The campaign as a whole lasted about half a year, from the second to the ninth month. The surviving records of prisoners and of the details of the siege are fragmentary and the numbers cannot be checked one by one, so wherever men or stores are mentioned above only the order of magnitude is given, and no exact assertion is made.
cause: 打起來有遠因，也有近因。遠因是宋夏戰爭三十餘年積累下來的邊境態勢：宋軍在好水川、定川寨一役連敗之後，河西走廊的三州落入西夏之手，絲路斷絕，兩國的商貿與使節往來幾乎中斷；熙寧年間宋廷在熙河開闢，取得河湟之地，側翼的基地算是站住了，但正面的靈州與河套仍在西夏手中，構成一個攻不下的突出部。兩個國家都清楚，只要靈州一天握在西夏手裡，宋朝的河湟就是懸在敵前的孤地。近因出在西夏內部：元豐三年諒祚與母后沒臧氏爭權，諒祚廢黜並幽禁母后、清除反對的臣將，宮廷清洗的消息傳到汴京，神宗判斷西夏的統治機器正在失靈，這是十幾年來唯一一次可以五路同時動手的窗口。戰略層面，王韶的方案是要用河湟的兵順著黃河東岸往下壓，把靈州從西夏的門戶變成宋朝的進攻跳板；只要靈州到手，西夏就必須把河套與河西的守軍抽回來應付，宋朝再以河湟為基地逐步向涼州、甘州施壓。至於直接動手的名義，則是邊境衝突與外交僵局：宋夏對米脂、綏德一線的歸屬與互市一直各執一詞，西夏扣留宋使、拒絕交涉，宋廷據此判定西夏已經撕毀前約，可以用兵。於是一場本可以作為劃界之爭解決的衝突，被推成了傾盡國力的總攻。
causeEn: There were remote causes and a proximate one. The remote cause was the frontier situation built up over more than thirty years of Song–Western Xia war: after the Song were beaten at Haoshuichuan and Dingchuanzhai, the three prefectures of the Hexi Corridor fell into Western Xia's hands, the silk road was cut, and intercourse between the two states almost ceased. When the Song opened up Xihé in the Xining era and gained ground in Hedong, the flanking base was secure, but Lingzhou and the Hetao were still in Western Xia's hands, forming a salient that could not be attacked. Both countries understood perfectly that as long as Lingzhou remained with Western Xia, the Song's Hedong was an outpost hanging in front of the enemy. The proximate cause lay inside Western Xia. In the third year of Yuanfeng, Liangzuo quarrelled with his mother, the Empress Dowager Maozang; he deposed and shut away the empress dowager and purged the courtiers who opposed him, and when the news of the palace purge reached Bianjing the emperor judged that the Western Xia machine of government was failing — the one window in a dozen years in which five routes could march at once. Strategically, Wang Shao's scheme was to use the troops in Hedong to press down the eastern bank of the Yellow River and turn Lingzhou from Western Xia's gateway into the Song's springboard; once Lingzhou was taken, Western Xia would have to draw the garrisons of the Hetao and Hexi back to meet the threat, and the Song could then press gradually towards Liangzhou and Ganzhou from its Hedong base. The immediate occasion was a combination of frontier incidents and a diplomatic deadlock: the Song and Western Xia had never agreed on the ownership of the Mizhi and Suide line or on the terms of mutual trade, Western Xia detained Song envoys and refused to negotiate, and the court at Bianjing judged on that basis that Western Xia had torn up the previous agreements and could be fought. In this way a dispute that might have been settled by a frontier demarcation was pushed into a general offensive costing both sides everything they had.
impact: 這場戰爭的影響不在靈州被佔了多久，而在它暴露了宋朝西北體制的幾處瓶頸。第一，戰爭證明以募兵為主、兵將分離的宋軍在遠距離攻勢下最脆弱的不是戰鬥力，而是轉運：靈州得手之後無法長期固守，糧車隊一旦被騎兵切斷，遠征軍就會在半路崩潰，第五都就是這樣一個教訓。第二，熙河、河湟的成果沒有被放棄，反而因為這次失敗而看得更重：元豐之後宋廷把陝西四塞的屯田、弓箭手屯戍與馬政整頓列為要務，河湟由軍屯變成國家長期經營的邊地，靈州則仍然像一枚楔子釘在西夏的腹心。第三，政治上這是一個轉折點：神宗好戰而起的五路大軍無功而返，保守派在朝議中抬頭，司馬光、文彥博等人借邊事失利質疑開邊之策，元祐更化的種子就在此時埋下；雖然熙河之地終未被棄，但宋朝對西夏的戰略從主攻轉為守禦。第四，從技術上看，這是一條值得與拜占庭對照的曲線：拜占庭把燃燒劑做成帝國壟斷的機密武器，最後因配方與訓練斷絕而在十二世紀消失；宋夏雙方卻在同一年裡大量使用火矢、火藥器械與噴射油膏的燃燒武器，燃燒技術正在從壟斷走向普及。第五，靈州之爭並未結束，此後近半個世紀裡宋夏在河套反覆拉鋸，靈州最終留在西夏手裡，成為它最後的核心，直到一二二七年蒙古滅夏。
impactEn: The effect of the war lies less in how long Lingzhou was held than in the bottlenecks it exposed in the Song military system in the northwest. First, it showed that what was weakest in a Song army raised by recruitment, with officers and men separated, was not fighting power in a distant offensive but movement and supply: once Lingzhou was taken it could not be held for long, and when the grain convoys were cut by horsemen the expeditionary force came apart on the road, which is precisely the lesson of Fifth Prefecture. Second, the gains in Xihé and Hedong were not abandoned; if anything the defeat made them more precious. After Yuanfeng the court put the registration of military farms, the settlement of archer households on the frontier and the reform of the horse administration in Shaanxi's four garrisons on the list of urgent business; Hedong changed from a campaigning base into a border district the state farmed over the long term, while Lingzhou remained a wedge driven into Western Xia's belly. Third, this was a political turning point: the five armies raised by an emperor fond of war came home without their object, the conservative voices gained ground in the discussions of the court, and Sima Guang and Wen Yanbo used the failure on the frontier to question the policy of opening new ground. The seed of the Yuanyou reaction was planted at that moment; the ground in Hedong was in the end never given up, but the Song strategy against Western Xia turned from attack into defence. Fourth, in technological terms this was a curve worth setting against the Byzantine one: Byzantium turned its burning charge into a monopolised imperial secret and lost it when the formula and the training were broken, so that it disappeared in the twelfth century, while on both sides of the Song–Western Xia war fire arrows, gunpowder devices and projected oil-grease burners were in wide use in the same year, and combustion technology was moving from monopoly towards ubiquity. Fifth, the contest over Lingzhou was not over. The Song and Western Xia fought for the Hetao back and forth for nearly half a century afterwards; Lingzhou ultimately stayed in Western Xia's hands and became its last core, until the Mongols destroyed the Xia state in 1227.
result: 結果是宋軍打了個不完整的勝仗。靈州城確實被攻破，宋軍一度立於黃河東岸，可以望見興慶府的城郭，但西夏用騎兵切斷糧道、在第五都吃掉河東路主力的辦法奏效，宋廷在九月下令撤退，諸路退回環慶、鄜延一線，靈州重新落入西夏治理，後來定名西平府，成為西夏在興慶府之外最要害的一處要地。河湟的收穫則保住了：熙河一路在同期取得的吐蕃聚落與城砦未在戰後歸還，宋朝在河湟的經營一直延續到徽宗朝。西夏雖然保住了靈州，卻在這一輪消耗中損失了精騎與漢兵，元氣受損，境內又經歷了諒祚的宮廷清洗，政令往往不能暢行到底，防守的重心不得不從前線堡寨退到興慶府周圍。對宋夏兩國來說，靈州從此成為一段反覆拉鋸、卻誰也吃不掉對方的地帶；對整個歐亞大陸的技術史來說，這一年同時記錄了兩件事：拜占庭的燃燒秘密走到盡頭，而東方的火藥與燃燒器械開始向戰場普及。
resultEn: The result was an incomplete victory for the Song. Lingzhou was genuinely stormed, and the Song stood for a time on the eastern bank of the Yellow River with the walls of Xingqing in sight across the water; but Western Xia's method worked — cutting the supply lines with cavalry and destroying the Hedong route at Fifth Prefecture — and in the ninth month the court ordered the withdrawal. The various routes fell back towards Huanqing and Fuyan, Lingzhou passed once more into Western Xia administration and was later given the name Xiping prefecture, becoming the most important strategic place the Xia state possessed outside Xingqing. The gains in Hedong, on the other hand, were kept: the Tibetan strongholds and forts taken by the Xihé route in the same campaign were not given back, and the Song administration of Hedong continued into the reign of Huizong. Western Xia kept Lingzhou but paid for it in elite cavalry and Han troops, and with the palace purge under Liangzuo the state came out of the war worn, its decrees often failing to reach the frontier, and the defensive centre of gravity withdrawn from the forward forts to the neighbourhood of Xingqing. For both the Song and Western Xia, Lingzhou became a stretch of ground over which they pulled at each other endlessly without either being able to swallow the other. In the wider history of Eurasian technology, the same year recorded two things at once: the Byzantine burning secret running to its end, and the spread of gunpowder and incendiary devices in the East.
